one_month_reasoning: 2026-11-01 is a Sunday, so the relevant close is Friday 2026-10-30. Lattice's Q3 report is not yet scheduled. Q3 2025 was reported on Nov 3 and calendars show Nov 3, 2026, so it very likely falls after the window. Events inside the window: (1) Aspeed's September monthly sales (~Oct 7-10). Aspeed guides to sequential growth through 2H26, so a strong print is mostly expected. (2) TSMC Q3 results (~Oct 15) and late-October hyperscaler earnings with 2027 capex commentary; these are positive on balance but known. (3) The AMI financials 8-K/A, due about mid-October. (4) The first AMI lock-up tranche: about 1.19M shares (25% of 4,741,352), tradable from Mon Oct 26, about 0.8% of shares outstanding. THL also holds block-trade rights. This is a small negative. (5) Pre-earnings positioning into a Q3 guide that is ~65% y/y FPGA-only growth. The overhang offsets the positioning, so I keep a near-symmetric lognormal centred at ~$134.4 with monthly sigma ~16.8% (61%/3.5, trimmed slightly because no company print is in the window).

fair_value.method: Blend of forward P/E (CY2028E EPS $3.80 x 36x = $137, weight 0.6) and EV/NTM sales (13x on ~$1.52B NTM revenue at Oct-2027 = $19.8B EV, less ~$0.55B net debt, over 146M diluted shares = $132, weight 0.4), which gives ~$135.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: CY2028E non-GAAP EPS $3.80 x 36x (the forward multiple I expect the market to apply in Oct-2027); 2027E EPS $3.12 at 4-6% tax and 146M diluted shares

inputs_detail.input: Non-GAAP tax rate, opex, gross margin guide (Q3-26)
inputs_detail.value: tax 4-6%; opex $83-90M with 2 months of AMI; GM ~69.5%

inputs_detail.derivation: Revenue $1.33B (FPGA ~$1.09B plus AMI ~$0.24B) x ~70% GM = ~$930M. Opex ~$420M (Q3 guide run-rated to a full AMI quarter of ~$100M, growing modestly) gives ~$510M operating income. Interest of ~$40M net on the $925M amortizing term loan gives ~$470M pretax; at 5% tax that is ~$447M over 146M diluted shares = ~$3.06. I land between this and the $3.21 consensus, since 2026 operating leverage has repeatedly beaten builds like this.

$3.12 grown ~22%. AI-server unit growth slows (TrendForce sees CSP capex growth easing from ~90% in 2026 to ~50% in 2027), but distributor demand is still broadening (Avnet guides +10% q/q and book-to-bill is above 1 in all regions) and FPGA supply is on allocation into 2027. Lower interest from deleveraging adds ~2%.

The historical mean is ~49x (TIKR, single source), and today the stock is ~43x my 2027E. I compress to 36x for decelerating growth in late 2027, the lower-growth AMI software mix and cycle risk (see the distributor-stocking discussion). I also lift the multiple 1x versus round 1 because AMI's ~75% GM / ~40% EBITDA mix with lower capital intensity deserves at least a semi-average premium.

methods.name: EV/sales
methods.inputs: NTM revenue at Oct-2027 ~$1.52B x 13x = $19.8B EV, less ~$0.55B net debt, / 146M diluted shares

inputs_detail.value: >$200M CY2026, ~75% GM, ~40% adj. EBITDA margin; ~+25% expected in 2027 per Q2 call

inputs_detail.derivation: 2027 consensus is $1.33B; the CEO's oral $1.2B exit-2026 run rate is a floor. NTM at the horizon spans Q4'27-Q3'28, so I take ~+15% over 2027. That is up from $1.45B in round 1 because the channel evidence is firmer than I assumed: Avnet inventory days are at a ~4-year low of 71 and its book-to-bill is above 1, and FPGA lead times run 40-52+ weeks with vendors prioritizing AI lines.

Today's EV is ~$20.4B ($134 x ~146M diluted plus ~$0.8B net debt), ~15x 2027E sales. I compress to 13x NTM (up from 12x in round 1). At a ~42% blended EBITDA margin, 13x sales is ~31x EBITDA, which reconciles with the 36x P/E leg (the supervisor flagged the $117 vs $138 gap).

$925M drawn on 2026-07-27 against ~$100-130M cash left after closing gives ~$0.8B now. Combined FCF is ~$100-120M/qtr (Q2 FPGA-only FCF $81M at 40% margin plus AMI). I assume some buyback resumption under the CFO's loose '<2x EBITDA by end-2027' target, so the figure lands a bit above the supervisor's $0.5B.
142,030,272 outstanding on 7/30/2026 already includes the 4,741,352 AMI shares; add RSUs and dilution.

bear.story: Lead-time-driven ordering unwinds. With FPGA lead times at 40-52 weeks and 95% of Lattice revenue through distributors, customers have placed orders ahead. Once AMD/Altera supply loosens or AI-server capex digests in mid-2027, a 2024-style channel destock begins (2024 revenue fell ~30%). 2028 EPS expectations fall to ~$2.8 and the multiple drops to ~28x.

base.story: FPGA grows ~20-25% on AI-server control/security attach plus an industrial recovery the distributors confirm, and AMI grows ~20%+ to plan. 2027 EPS is ~$3.1-3.2, CY2028E ~$3.8, and the multiple compresses to ~36x, so the stock ends modestly above today.

bull.story: AI/custom-ASIC rack growth stays at 30%+ into 2028, Lattice takes control-FPGA share while Xilinx/Altera are on allocation, and AMI BMC/BIOS cross-sells to hyperscalers. NTM revenue runs above $1.7B, EPS ~$4.7, and the premium ~45x multiple holds.

thesis_break_reason: ~$85 (-37%) is ~27x my 2027E EPS of $3.12 and ~20% below the Aug-Sep 2026 lows of $104-111. Trading there would most likely mean a fundamental break, not 60% vol: either a guide-down showing that the 'booked' 2027 was lead-time-driven distributor ordering (distributors are 95% of revenue, two of them hold 88% of receivables), an AI-server capex digestion, or AMI BMC/BIOS share loss. Value-chain tells to watch: Aspeed monthly sales turning negative y/y, Avnet/Arrow book-to-bill falling below 1 or inventory days rising sharply from 71, and FPGA lead times collapsing back toward 8-12 weeks. I keep $85 rather than the supervisor's $88: the difference is within noise, and my bear case already sits at $78.

reasoning: Round 2 changes are driven by the supervisor's findings plus four in-lane checks. Facts corrected or confirmed: (a) 2027 consensus of $3.21 is fine, but my own guidance-arithmetic build (4-6% tax, ~146M diluted shares, ~$40M net interest) gives ~$3.06, so I use $3.12 and CY2028E $3.80 (was $3.95). (b) Net debt at Oct-2027 is ~$0.55B, not $0.7B, because combined FCF is ~$400-480M/yr. (c) My round-1 source 14 was mislabelled; it was the Q2 press release, and I now cite the SEC copy instead of a Webull reprint. The supervisor asked what the industry evidence says about distributor stocking versus end demand at 95% distributor mix. Avnet's June-quarter release shows sales +48% y/y, book-to-bill above 1 in all regions and inventory days at 71, the lowest in nearly four years. Fusion Worldwide (2026-07-31) reports FPGA lead times of 40-52+ weeks, ~30% fill rates at AMD/Xilinx, and Lattice prioritizing AI lines. My read: the channel is lean, not stuffed, so 2027 shipments are well supported (bull for the next 2-3 quarters). But long lead times plus allocation are the classic setup for double ordering, which unwinds when supply loosens, as in the 2023-24 FPGA destock. That risk sits mostly in mid-2027 to 2028, so it stays inside the horizon and keeps the bear weight at 25% rather than shrinking it. Valuation: P/E $137 (36x $3.80) and EV/sales $132 (13x $1.52B less $0.55B net debt), now reconciled (13x sales is ~31x EBITDA at a 42% margin). Blended fair value is $135 (from $130), close to the supervisor's ~$140 but reached independently. I hold it a little lower because I weight the channel cycle risk more. Scenarios 25/50/25 at $78/$138/$215 (probability-weighted ~$142). Ladder: a mixture of 82% lognormal (median $138, sigma 0.47) and 18% wide component (median $130, sigma 0.85) to keep fat tails, giving P(>=134) 0.517, about 1 point above round 1 mid-ladder. Research this round was limited to ~5 queries; X/social sources were not used.
